q: How does a Tiruppur dyeing unit count emissions from a firewood boiler?
title: Tiruppur dyeing: firewood boiler emissions
short: CO2 from burning wood is biogenic: report it separately, outside the scopes. Methane and nitrous oxide from the burning still count in Scope 1. With IPCC defaults, a tonne of firewood gives about 1.75 t of biogenic CO2 and about 0.03 t CO2e of Scope 1 gases.
audience: Dyeing and processing units with firewood or wood-chip boilers in the Tiruppur cluster of Tamil Nadu

ul: Net calorific value of wood: 15.6 GJ per tonne (IPCC 2006 Vol 2, Table 1.2).
CO2: 112,000 kg per TJ, reported as biogenic.
CH4: 30 kg per TJ and N2O: 4 kg per TJ (Table 2.3).
GWP: 27.0 for non-fossil methane and 273 for N2O (IPCC AR6).

p: Keep purchase invoices by weight. If the wood is bought by volume or by the cart, record the conversion you used and its source.

example.title: Worked example: 10 tonnes of firewood (IPCC defaults)
lines: Energy: 10 t x 15.6 GJ = 156 GJ = 0.156 TJ
Biogenic CO2: 0.156 x 112,000 = 17,472 kg, reported outside the scopes
example.note: The fuel quantity is illustrative; the factors are IPCC defaults.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.

sources.label: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Chapter 7 (GWP values)
